steps.title: Oral fluid reaches a real epithelial pore
steps.camera: Vallate wall and true pore: intact
steps.text: Tastants dissolve in oral fluid and reach the apical microvillar region through the small true taste pore in an otherwise continuous epithelial wall. The trench is an external cleft; it is not the pore. No particle is modeled entering a nerve or crossing the whole epithelium.
steps.micro_focus_limit: Existing lesson focus only. It ghosts others and queues reframing; use the companion adapter for a matched authored-camera/context sequence.
steps.check_question: Which opening is the true taste pore, and which is the surrounding trench?

steps.title: Open an explanatory window while retaining its host
steps.text: A named tissue window reveals epithelial cell bodies, nuclei, apical microvilli and basal neural apposition. The removed wall/cell caps are teaching removals, not natural perforations. Receptor, supporting and basal colors identify schematic representatives; no molecular Type II/III identity is proved by these meshes.
steps.micro_focus_limit: Existing lesson focus only. It ghosts others and queues reframing; use the companion adapter for a matched authored-camera/context sequence.

steps.title: Narrate a Type II sweet/bitter/umami example
steps.text: For a Type II example, an apical taste GPCR activates an intracellular signaling cascade involving PLC-beta2, intracellular calcium and TRPM5-dependent depolarization. TRPM5 conducts monovalent cations, not calcium. Sweet, bitter and umami use distinct receptor populations; this generic receptor selector does not encode all three identities in one cell. Molecular events are narration, not visible resolved organelles.
steps.micro_focus_limit: Existing lesson focus only. It ghosts others and queues reframing; use the companion adapter for a matched authored-camera/context sequence.

steps.title: Transfer a cell signal to a separate sensory terminal
steps.text: In Type II cells, depolarization/action potentials open a basolateral CALHM1/CALHM3 ATP-release channel. ATP activates purinergic receptors on a separate gustatory afferent. This is channel-mediated transmitter release, not a conventional vesicular Type II synapse; it occurs at a basal/lateral neural interface, not through the apical taste pore. The drawn terminal is a representative apposition, not ultrastructural channel proof.
steps.micro_focus_limit: Existing lesson focus only. It ghosts others and queues reframing; use the companion adapter for a matched authored-camera/context sequence.
steps.check_question: Why is the epithelial receptor cell distinct from the nerve fiber?

steps.title: Compare a Type III sour example without conflating release routes
steps.text: For a separate Type III example, acidic stimuli activate OTOP1-mediated proton entry and depolarization; voltage-dependent calcium entry can trigger vesicular serotonin release at conventional contacts. Purinergic signaling also contributes to sour afferent transmission; a complete universal sour ATP-release route is not resolved here. These findings rely heavily on mouse experiments. No Type III-specific morphology or membrane current is represented in this sampled mesh.
steps.micro_focus_limit: Existing lesson focus only. It ghosts others and queues reframing; use the companion adapter for a matched authored-camera/context sequence.

steps.title: Distinguish cranial sensory routes and motor supply
steps.text: The circumvallate example is associated with IX. Taste from anterior fungiform buds travels with chorda tympani fibers of VII carried by the lingual nerve; ordinary anterior tongue sensation is carried by V3 fibers, which are not separately resolved in this selector. XII is motor to intrinsic muscle, not a taste afferent. The recovered construction does not establish new foliate sensory endings or a brainstem circuit.
steps.micro_focus_limit: Existing lesson focus only. It ghosts others and queues reframing; use the companion adapter for a matched authored-camera/context sequence.

Cell classes are a teaching taxonomy. Nineteen sampled cells are not a complete or measured bud population.
No regional tongue taste-quality map or universal human salt-transduction scheme is implied.

steps.title: Read interwoven fascicles and their connective partitions
steps.text: Interlacing skeletal-muscle fascicles occur in several directions. Perimysial connective partitions and interstitial adipocytes are different tissues. The tissue is dense and interwoven; simplified orthogonal samples must not be read as a repetitive rigid lattice or as independent actuators. The first recovered candidate remains visually rejected for its regular sleeves/lattice.

steps.title: Compare superior and inferior longitudinal examples
steps.text: Longitudinal contraction contributes to shortening and bending the tongue. Superior and inferior longitudinal examples contribute differently to upward versus downward curvature; actual shape depends on coordinated neighboring intrinsic and extrinsic fibers and boundary conditions. These static fascicles do not shorten on screen.

steps.title: Relate transverse orientation to narrowing and elongation
steps.text: Transverse fibers cross from the septal region toward the lateral margins. Their shortening contributes to narrowing and lengthening of the muscular tongue. This local histology block does not establish whole-tongue protrusion or determine displacement by itself.

steps.title: Relate vertical orientation to flattening and broadening
steps.text: Vertical fibers contribute to flattening and broadening when coordinated with the rest of the tongue. Orientation can be compared in sections, but a source-only static sample does not compute volume conservation, fascicle strain or the shape of a spoken sound.

steps.title: Distinguish a motor terminal target from taste innervation
steps.text: XII motor fibers supply intrinsic skeletal muscle. The sampled branch approaches a muscle example and is distinct from taste afferents reaching epithelial buds. An isolated cable or small spray does not prove a neuromuscular junction; acetylcholine release, endplate receptors, excitation-contraction coupling and sarcomere shortening are not structurally resolved here.
